patch_description: The current `balanced_packing` runs a Python-level loop over all items, but each iteration performs several full-row tensor operations (`torch.where`, `argmin`, two `scatter_`, fancy indexing). That is O(n) tensor kernel launches per row — the dominant cost of the whole algorithm (it is called twice per rebalance). Replacing it with a classic heapq-based LPT packer operating on plain Python lists removes all per-item tensor kernel launches while producing an identical (or better, due to deterministic tie-breaking) assignment. Since weights are already moved to CPU as the first operation of `rebalance_experts`, pure-Python list arithmetic is very fast at these problem sizes (tens of layers, hundreds of experts). Likewise, `replicate_experts` performs `num_redundant` iterations of tensor ops (`argmax`, gather, index updates); converting it to a per-row Python greedy with lists eliminates those kernel launches too. This keeps the exact same greedy semantics (clone the expert with the highest per-replica load) but with far lower overhead, directly improving `times_algorithm` / `speed_score` without touching the resulting balancedness scores. Per the reliability recommendation, `weight = weight.float().cpu()` stays the first operation in the entry point, all intermediate tensors remain on CPU, and `torch.sort(..., descending=True)` (no newer kwargs) is used for the initial ordering.
